definition: Exactly four existing account clauses: S contains x; every S member holds at w; every admitted reason for an S member belongs to S; each contingent S member has an admitted reason. The original ReasonClosed nonCopy clause is omitted.
note: Transparent weakening of existing shared explanatory vocabulary, not a new ontology or definition of adequate explanation. ofReasonClosed checks the original-to-weaker projection. Coverage still excludes a contingent unexplained account member by stipulation, not independent defense. Founded and both fixed-constituent policies remain separate OPEN inputs. Ordinary reason examples orient the reading but do not establish universal coverage or real constituency; brute contingent stops, non-well-founded accounts and necessary abstract facts remain serious rival policies. No causal direction, modal sufficiency, structural asymmetry, source correspondence or reality applicability follows.
